newsitem.title: UK: London freight - Panamax business firm in most areas.
newsitem.headline: London freight - Panamax business firm in most areas.

text.p: Panamax business has been completed at firm levels in most areas, especially period timecharters of between 3-5 and 7-9 months.
This has been despite a low volume of fixtures reported on Monday, which was accounted for by Far Eastern holidays and imminent ones in Brazil and elsewhere.
Caper and handy markets have remained dull.
GRAIN - Talk circulated of Finagrain booking the 1976-built Toscana 63,159 dwt delivery Passero mid Feb for 12 months at $9,500 daily.
This was reckoned by brokers to be a firm rate for an over-age vessel, especially if redelivery is Atlantic and not worldwide.
In the east the 1989-built Antonis I Angelicoussis 69,346 dwt was understood to be working closely delivery Japan end Feb for 7-9 months at about $11,500/11,750 daily.
While the Oinoussian Navigator 64,348 dwt for a similar period delivery prompt Taiwan done for about $1,000 daily less, both probably for S.Korean account.
El Flamenco 69,351 dwt was thought fixed delivery Far East for 12 months at $11,000/11,250 daily to unnamed charterers.
There were also reports of the 1980-built Koyo-type Merchant Pilot 58,371 dwt working 12 months business delivery Continent mid Feb at close to $9,750 daily.

Trip timecharters from the east coast south America to the Continent were said to have been fixed by Pioneer with an unidentified panamax at $15,900 daily, and by Saroc with the 1973-built Zouzou 50,947 dwt spot Recalada trip Med at about $7,000 daily.
A handy-size was reported booked for 22,000 grain Plate/Las Palmas at $22.00.
Continental was rumoured to have fixed a panamax (possibly Paramos) for U.S. Gulf/west Med and also 25,000 grains U.S Gulf/Turkey, both on private terms.

New orders quoted today include Glencore 50/60,000 heavy grain Mississippi/Spanish Med for Feb 20/March 3, Iranians 100,000 corn (try 2 bottoms of 50,000 dwcc each), Argentina/Iran for March/April, Cargill 25,000 wheat north France/Algeria for Feb 25/March 3, and Andre 25,000 wheat Rouen/Port Sudan for Feb 24/March 3.

Minerals were a very quiet market. British Steel was believed to have booked a caper for ironore from Ponta da Madeira to Port Talbot on private terms, and Ankerkolen was said to have failed on subjects with 120,000 coal Richards Bay/Rotterdam for March at $6.75.
